introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2025. Duration: Two and a Half Hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.
enonce_intro_markdown: A particle, $P$, executes simple harmonic motion along a straight line with centre $O$. The period of motion is $2\pi$ seconds and the amplitude is $5$ metres. Initially, $P$ passes through the point $A$ while moving with velocity $-3\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Find,
incertitudes: Question 3 (ii) : le sujet ne précise pas de quel côté de O se trouve A. La vitesse initiale étant -3 m/s (vers O si A est du côté positif), A est pris à x = +4 m : le trajet « directement de A à O » n'a de sens que si P se dirige vers O. Par symétrie, le résultat (0.9273 s) est identique si l'on place A de l'autre côté avec la vitesse orientée vers O.

questions.corrige_markdown:
The period is $T = 2\pi$ s, so the angular frequency is $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T} = 1\ \mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}$. The amplitude is $a = 5$ m.

For SHM the speed at displacement $x$ from the centre satisfies $v^2 = \omega^2(a^2 - x^2)$. At $A$ the speed is $3\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ (the velocity is $-3$), so

$$9 = 1^2\,(25 - x^2)\ \Longrightarrow\ x^2 = 16\ \Longrightarrow\ x = \pm 4.$$

Hence $OA = 4\ \mathrm{m}$.
themes: simple harmonic motion of a particle

questions.enonce_markdown: the time, in seconds, to four significant figures, taken by $P$ to move directly from $A$ to $O$. *[8 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Measure the displacement $x$ from $O$. The velocity at $A$ is negative, so $P$ is moving towards $O$ and $A$ is at $x = +4$ (a particle that is at $x=-4$ with velocity $-3$ would be moving away from $O$, and would not go "directly" from $A$ to $O$).

With $\omega = 1$ the general solution is $x = 5\cos(t + \varepsilon)$, so $v = \dot x = -5\sin(t+\varepsilon)$.

Initial conditions at $t = 0$:

$$5\cos\varepsilon = 4,\qquad -5\sin\varepsilon = -3\ \Longrightarrow\ \cos\varepsilon = \tfrac45,\ \sin\varepsilon = \tfrac35,\ \varepsilon = \arccos\tfrac45 = 0.6435\ \text{rad}.$$

$P$ reaches $O$ for the first time when $x = 0$, that is $\cos(t+\varepsilon) = 0$ with $t + \varepsilon = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$:

$$t = \frac{\pi}{2} - \arccos\frac45 = \arcsin\frac45 = 0.9273\ \text{s}\ \ (4\ \text{s.f.})$$

Check by symmetry: starting from $O$ with $x = 5\sin t$, the point $x = 4$ is reached when $\sin t = \tfrac45$, giving the same time $t = 0.9273$ s.

The time taken is $0.9273$ s.
themes: simple harmonic motion of a particle
